chapter: Union, publishers, race and Harlem nightlife
title: Margaret and the Bill Robinson incident
summary: Mrs. H tells how Bill Robinson drew a gold pistol on a drunk who bumped her and Sid Catlett calmed him.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Nobody knows what happened. Nobody knew whatever happened because when we got to the cafeteria... Jay had to go
out on a little errand. So Sid Catlett and I were sitting in the restaurant. We were waiting for our train to come in. I'll tell you who else was up there was Rogers, the comedian.
I was with Timmy Rogers a couple of days ago.

Yes, Timmy Rogers was up there. There was a whole lot of them up there. So anyhow, I went up to the cafeteria to get a sandwich and Bill Robinson came up and there was a white man standing there. He was high and he fell up against me. So nobody was paying Bill Robinson no mind. So he going to make a big splash - (BELL RINGS) - that's my kids.
The worst one - never in my life - I never hate nobody. People I don't like, I pray for them, but I can't stand this - every time I look at him I want to fight him so bad just one time.
Tell me, all of these things like you're talking about Bill Robinson and things about Louis Armstrong - did any of these things have any effect on your playing?
(THIS IS NOT CLEAR AS PEOPLE ARE COMING IN OR LEAVING.)
Anyway, I think I was at the restaurant counter. Jay had gone on an errand. So Sidney Catlett and I were sitting at the table and I ordered a sandwich and Jay came back.

We were getting ready to make the train back to New York. So Bill Robinson comes up to the place. There's this white fellow. He was high. Well, he, you know, knocked up against me. I didn't pay him no mind. So Bill Robinson said - you know we were youngsters then, very young. So he said, "Is this man molesting you?" Nobody had recognized Bill Robinson, so he's going to take it out on me to be recognized, and that's what I didn't like and neither did Sid Catlett. I said, "No, he's not molesting me. The man is just high and he fell up against me." "Oh, I'll take out my gold pistol," and he did take it out. He had a gold pistol. So Sid Catlett came up to him. He said, "Now listen, let Margaret alone. Let her come on back and sit down and get her sandwich and let her alone." Somebody told Jay about the incident. We all got on the train coming back to New York. So he came over and he begged my pardon, he really did. He said, "I'm sorry." I said, "But you didn't have no business to make me, you know, make a fool out of me so you could be recognized." ...

I said, "Why pick on me; I'm nobody." ... When Jay heard about it we had to quiet him down... "Why did you pick on Margaret to make yourself famous?" He was already famous; he didn't have to do that to me.
because he was going to whip on everybody.
He was just going to make a spectacle -
Out of himself and make me look like a fool. We were all up there for fun, Tim Rogers and all. Even Tim Rogers remembered the incident. He may not remember me, but he may
remember the incident. Midge Williams - did you ever hear of Midge Williams?
